stage_1_input_echo.description: Baseline field observations using everyday measures.

items.observation: Reddish, coarse, gravelly topsoil with a hard subsurface layer encountered within hand's depth (~10 cm).

stage_2_missing_analysis.description: Separation of observations, inferences, and unknowns.

items.observation: Hard crust stops standard hand trowel penetration; reddish gravel texture.
items.inference: Shallow iron/aluminum oxide accumulation restricts root growth and accelerates surface runoff.
items.unknown: Exact chemical pH level and precise mineral saturation depth.
items.limitations_risks: Assuming uniform soil depth across the plateau without spot-checking.

stage_3_fix_protocol.description: Condition-dependent soil preparation and runoff management.

items.action: Do not attempt deep plowing. Target hardpan breaking at grid points spaced 2 paces apart using heavy hand tools. Apply 1 bucketful of organic compost or decomposed leaf litter per planting pit to buffer acidity.
Incorporate organic matter (2 bucketfuls per square pace) and establish stone contour bunds to stabilize gravel.
Dig shallow contour trenches (one hand's depth deep) across the slope every 3 paces to capture and infiltrate heavy rainfall.
Construct raised planting beds or ridges (hand's depth high) to prevent waterlogging around root zones during intense rain bursts.

observable_checks: Sturdy hand tool penetrates easily to hand's depth (~15 cm) after organic amendment.
Bucketful water test shows water is absorbed within the planting pocket rather than instantly washing away.
items.pass_meaning: Soil structure is sufficiently amended to support root expansion and moisture retention.
items.fail_meaning: Soil still resists tool penetration or water runs off instantly; re-apply Fix Protocol.

stage_5_crop_suggestions.description: Condition-appropriate adaptive crop choices and trade-offs.

items.suitability: High tolerance for acidic, gravelly soils and moderate dry periods.
items.trade_offs: Lower yield on untreated hardpan; requires localized organic pocket amendment.

items.suitability: Deep taproot helps fracture sub-surface layers over time; fixes nitrogen.
Thrives on mounded ridge systems that prevent waterlogging on flat pooling terrain.
Resilient against unexpected dry spells and late rainy season starts.
items.trade_offs: Sensitive to extreme waterlogging if drainage fails.

stage_6_timeframe.description: Remediation buffers and realistic crop maturity ranges.

items.remediation_buffer: 3 to 7 days for organic composting and crust fracturing.
items.seasonal_adjustment: Adjust sowing schedule when late rains delay the rainy season start.

stage_7_planting_method.description: Micro-catchments, bed preparation, and sowing depth.

items.method: Plant in zai pits or half-moon micro-catchments spaced 2 paces apart along contour lines to harvest scarce rainfall.
items.sowing_depth: Shallow depth (approx. one finger-joint) to allow easy emergence through amended topsoil pockets.

stage_8_ongoing_care.description: Staged fertility, mulching, and dry-spell care.

items.action: Apply organic mulch (dry leaf litter or grass) two hand-spans wide around plant bases to reduce moisture evaporation. Perform manual weeding early in the season to eliminate nutrient competition.
items.pest_monitoring: Inspect leaf undersides weekly; apply organic neem-based deterrents if pests appear.

stage_9_harvest_regeneration.description: Maturity signs, non-tillage harvest, and soil recovery.

items.harvest_signs: Grain hardening for millets, pod drying for pigeon peas, or tuber skin firming for sweet potatoes.
items.harvest_method: Harvest crops without deep tilling. Cut stalks cleanly at ground level to preserve soil aggregates.
items.regeneration_action: Retain crop stubble and incorporate organic green matter post-harvest to rebuild acidity-stressed soil structure.
